cross_modal_consistency.dimension_interpretation: The partition-level structural diagnostics describe how the eight current candidate sets are represented in the fused four-view patient geometry. Within-set affinity is uniformly high and tightly bounded (0.00965–0.01038) across sets of very different sizes (7–20 patients), indicating that each candidate set is internally cohesive in this geometry. The eigengap profiles are dominated by the first gap in every set: leading gaps of 0.061–0.156 are one to two orders of magnitude larger than the next gaps (e.g., 0.00018–0.0027), and all eight sets screen at candidate_k=1. This means the spectral screening calculation is dominated by the single-cluster resolution and does not identify a dominant multi-cluster subdivision signal within any current set; it does not provide feasible k>=2 set-level solutions to interpret. The nearest-pair affinities identify several relatively close candidate pairs (K8_C0004–K8_C0006, K8_C0002–K8_C0003, K8_C0006–K8_C0008, and pairs involving K8_C0001 with K8_C0006/K8_C0004/K8_C0008), but their between-set affinities (about 0.00905–0.00926) remain slightly below the within-set range, so these are pair-review entry points rather than evidence that the boundaries are absent. Overall, the measurements indicate that the current memberships are internally coherent in the fused geometry, with no dominant internal subdivision signal detected by this screening, while a subset of pairs is relatively close and may warrant closer boundary inspection. These are structural descriptions of the current partition, not conclusions about whether any set should be split or merged.

biological_support.dimension_interpretation: K8_C0001 shows a coherent and interpretable biological phenotype relative to the rest of the partition, dominated by coordinated down-regulation of oxidative phosphorylation (NES -1.97, FDR 0.001), adipogenesis (NES -1.72, FDR 0.005), fatty-acid metabolism (NES -1.64, FDR 0.009), and protein secretion (NES -1.63, FDR 0.009), with estrogen-response programs also down (NES -1.79, FDR 0.003). The leading-edge genes for oxidative phosphorylation include many mitochondrial and respiratory-chain genes (e.g., PDHA1, NDUFS1, COX5A, ATP5F1A), indicating a broad mitochondrial-metabolic signal rather than a single-gene effect. Up-regulated programs (MYC targets, E2F targets, EMT) are present but weaker and not significant after multiplicity correction, so the phenotype is primarily a metabolic-depletion profile. Because the rest group combines the other seven candidate sets, this contrast describes K8_C0001 against a heterogeneous background rather than against any single comparator.

cross_modal_consistency.dimension_interpretation: The partition-level structural diagnostics describe how the eight current candidate sets are represented in the fused four-view patient geometry. Within-set affinity is uniformly high and tightly bounded (0.00965–0.01038) across sets of very different sizes (7–20 patients), indicating that each candidate set is internally cohesive in this geometry. The eigengap profiles are dominated by the first gap in every set: leading gaps of 0.061–0.156 are one to two orders of magnitude larger than the next gaps (e.g., 0.00018–0.0027), and all eight sets screen at candidate_k=1. This means the spectral screening calculation is dominated by the single-cluster resolution and does not identify a dominant multi-cluster subdivision signal within any current set; it does not provide feasible k>=2 set-level solutions to interpret. The nearest-pair affinities identify several relatively close candidate pairs (K8_C0004–K8_C0006, K8_C0002–K8_C0003, K8_C0006–K8_C0008, and pairs involving K8_C0001 with K8_C0006/K8_C0004/K8_C0008), but their between-set affinities (about 0.00905–0.00926) remain slightly below the within-set range, so these are pair-review entry points rather than evidence that the boundaries are absent. Overall, the measurements indicate that the current memberships are internally coherent in the fused geometry, with no dominant internal subdivision signal detected by this screening, while a subset of pairs is relatively close and may warrant closer boundary inspection. reports.dimension_interpretation: The partition-level structural diagnostics describe how the eight current candidate sets are represented in the fused four-view patient geometry. reports.dimension_interpretation: Several measured technical and acquisition factors show statistically significant association with candidate membership at the partition level. Tissue source site is significantly associated (Cramer's V 0.258, q 0.003), with BP and B0/B8 contributing most of the imbalance. CT slice thickness (epsilon-squared 0.220, q 0.0011) and CT z-spacing (epsilon-squared 0.219, q 0.0011) are also significantly associated. CT phase, CT manufacturer, CT scanner model, CT reconstruction kernel, CT pixel spacing, and study year show no significant association after correction. These are associations, not proof of technical artifact or causation; the significant factors could plausibly account for part of the signal or geometry, but the analysis does not establish that they do. The categorical factors with many levels (scanner model, reconstruction kernel) have sparse cells, which limits power and stability. Because the partition has eight sets, the contingency tables are large and some cells are sparse, so the association estimates should be interpreted with caution.

In the fused geometry, tissue source site shows significant PERMANOVA location association (R-squared 0.050, q 0.0025) with no significant PERMDISP dispersion difference (q 0.434), so the association is primarily a location/centroid shift rather than a dispersion difference. In the CT native-distance geometry, CT phase (R-squared 0.154, q 0.0025), CT manufacturer (R-squared 0.059, q 0.0067), CT slice thickness (R-squared 0.136, q 0.002), CT z-spacing (R-squared 0.142, q 0.002), CT pixel spacing (R-squared 0.019, q 0.035), and study year (R-squared 0.029, q 0.004) all show significant associations. CT reconstruction kernel and CT scanner model show nominal PERMANOVA associations that do not survive correction (q 0.054), and their PERMDISP was not estimable due to sparse groups. These are associations, not proof of technical artifact or causation; the significant factors could plausibly account for part of the geometry, but the analysis does not establish that they do. The R-squared values are univariable and must not be added.
